root_cause.text: The imx8mp HDMI blk-ctrl power-domain code incorrectly gated the HDCP NoC clock (NOC_HDCP, bit 11) on power on/off of the HDCP domain, even though that clock must remain continuously enabled for the NoC ADB400 power-down handshake to complete safely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP cases that set/clear HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 BIT(11) in `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on()` and `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off()`, and instead unconditionally enables BIT(11) in `imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier()`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly says this is needed to “fix the potential hang caused by the NoC ADB400 port power down handshake.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop enabling the HDCP clock bit during HDMI block power-on for the HDCP domain.
intent_record.what: The switch case handling for IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP was removed from imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on(), deleting the regmap_set_bits(bc->regmap, HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0, BIT(11)) call and its break statement.
intent_record.how: At runtime, calling imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on() with IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP no longer sets BIT(11) in HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 in this function, so the HDCP-specific power-on clock enable action is no longer performed here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop clearing HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 bit 11 when powering off the HDCP block to avoid incorrect HDCP power-off behavior.
intent_record.what: The switch case handling IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP was removed from imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off(), deleting the call to regmap_clear_bits(bc->regmap, HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0, BIT(11)) for that power domain.
intent_record.how: At runtime, powering off the HDCP block no longer clears bit 11 in HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0, so this function stops disabling that specific clock/control bit during HDCP power-off handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set the missing HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 bit 11 during HDMI power-up to correct clock/control register initialization.
intent_record.what: The diff modifies a single regmap_set_bits() call in imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier() by adding BIT(11) to the bitmask previously containing BIT(0), BIT(1), and BIT(10) for the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes bit 11 of the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register to be set during the HDMI power notification sequence, enabling or configuring one additional clock-control flag that was previously left unset and thereby correcting the hardware initialization state.

Set the missing HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 bit 11 during HDMI power-up to correct clock/control register initialization.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 bit 11 handling so the register is correctly managed during HDMI/HDCP power state transitions.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause by stopping the HDCP NoC clock bit from being enabled/gated during HDCP domain power-on, matching the issue that this clock must remain continuously enabled for safe ADB400 handshake.

The changes directly modify handling of HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 bit 11 during HDCP/HDMI power transitions, which matches the root cause of incorrectly gating the HDCP NoC clock (bit 11) that must stay enabled for safe power-domain handshake.

candidates.rationale: This explicitly enables the HDCP NoC clock bit only during HDCP domain power-on, embodying the incorrect gating behavior described in the root cause. The clock must remain continuously enabled instead of being managed per-domain transition.
This clears the HDCP NoC clock bit during HDCP domain power-off, directly causing the unsafe disabling of a clock that must stay enabled for the NoC ADB400 power-down handshake to complete.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement disables the HDCP NoC clock during HDCP power-off. The root cause states that NOC_HDCP bit 11 must remain continuously enabled so the NoC ADB400 power-down handshake can complete safely, making this power-transition gating directly vulnerable.

This statement enables the HDCP NoC clock only as part of HDCP domain power-on, reflecting the incorrect design of gating bit 11 on domain transitions instead of leaving it continuously enabled as required by the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it fully shows the switch case for the HDCP power domain and the exact clock gating operation. In the `case IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP:` block, the code executes `regmap_clear_bits(bc->regmap, HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0, BIT(11));` at line 294. Per the stated root cause, `NOC_HDCP` is `BIT(11)` and must remain continuously enabled; gating it during HDCP domain power on/off is the vulnerable behavior. The presence of this clear operation in the HDCP domain handling means the vulnerable construct is present. There is no compensating logic here to keep `BIT(11)` enabled or to exclude `NOC_HDCP` from HDCP power-domain transitions, so the fix is not present.
